Abstract:
PURPOSE: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (MEC) and adenoid cystic carcinoma (AdCC) are the two most common salivary gland malignancies, but differ substantially in biological behavior, recurrence patterns and long-term prognosis. Comparative data from patients treated within the same institution using similar management strategies remain limited. This study compared long-term survival, recurrence patterns and prognostic factors between MEC and AdCC to identify histology-specific characteristics that may inform follow-up and treatment strategies. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients treated for MEC or AdCC at a tertiary academic center between 1996 and 2022. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS) and recurrence patterns, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: Sixty-two patients (31 AdCC, 31 MEC) were included. Although 5-year OS was identical (81%), AdCC had significantly poorer DFS (53% vs. 80%, p = 0.015) and higher recurrence rates (18/31 vs. 8/31, p = 0.020), and more distant metastases (18/31 vs. 1/31 patients, p = 0.0016). AdCC demonstrates more aggressive biology with higher recurrence rates and poorer DFS despite similar OS. The limited survival benefit of salvage therapy highlights the need for grade-adapted management and more effective therapies for high-grade disease.

item.title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of cerebrospinal fluid leak in skull base surgery: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: Aydogmus E, Atalay Erdogan B
item.description:
Authors: Aydogmus E, Atalay Erdogan B
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10667-1
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867660



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak remains one of the most significant complications of skull base surgery, particularly in endoscopic endonasal and transsphenoidal approaches. Accurate risk stratification may improve surgical planning and reconstruction strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have been increasingly investigated for CSF leak prediction; however, the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to map the current literature and summarize data sources, modeling approaches, validation strategies, and reported performance. METHODS: This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligibility was structured using the Population-Concept-Context framework. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published from 2019 to 2025. Two authors independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts and independently charted data using a standardized table; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Eligible original human studies applied AI/ML to predict perioperative surgical CSF leak or to derive an imaging biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak/encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. No formal protocol was prepared or registered. RESULTS: Fifty-five records were identified, and nine primary studies met the eligibility criteria after duplicate removal and full-text assessment. Six studies predicted intraoperative CSF leak, two predicted postoperative leak, and one evaluated a deep-learning-derived CT biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak or encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. Three studies used classical machine-learning methods, four used predominantly deep neural-network or convolutional-neural-network approaches, one compared classical models with a feedforward neural network, and one used a BERT-based natural-language-processing model. One study reported prospective temporal validation; none reported independent external validation at another institution. Among studies reporting AUC, values ranged from 0.69 to 1.00; accuracy, where reported, ranged from 70% to 98.33%. CONCLUSIONS: AI-based prediction of CSF leak is a promising but evolving field. Methodological heterogeneity and the absence of independent external validation constrain clinical translation. Future studies should prioritize standardized outcomes, multicenter datasets, and prospective validation to support integration into clinical decision-making.

item.title: Impact of early combined oral and intratympanic corticosteroid therapy on hearing outcomes in sudden sensorineural hearing loss: A prospective cohort study.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate hearing outcomes following early simultaneous oral and intratympanic corticosteroid therapy in patients with sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSHL). METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted including 65 adult patients with SSHL treated with oral prednisone (1 mg/kg/day; maximum 60 mg/day) for 14 days combined with intratympanic methylprednisolone (40 mg/mL) administered weekly for three weeks. RESULTS: Median baseline PTA improved from 85 dB to 56 dB one month after treatment, corresponding to a median improvement of 28 dB (p < 0.0001). Median SDS increased from 0% to 80% (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: Early simultaneous combined oral and intratympanic corticosteroid therapy was associated with significant improvements in PTA and SDS in this cohort of patients with SSHL without major adverse events observed during follow-up. Abstract:
PURPOSE: Thyroid cancers often present as nodules, with fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) and ultrasonography as the primary diagnostic tools. Given the variability in clinical approaches and the lack of consensus guidelines, ultrasonography has become increasingly important, particularly for indeterminate cytology. We aim to assess the clinical utility and diagnostic performance of the ACR TI-RADS (American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System), together with cytopathological subtypes, in predicting malignancy in atypia of undetermined significance (AUS) cases. METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre study conducted over 30 months, all AUS cases underwent preoperative ultrasonographic evaluation using the ACR TI-RADS, and had postoperative histopathological results. RESULTS: Seventy-one nodules from 67 patients were included. The median age was 51 years (range: 12-71). The overall malignancy rate was 20%. Among the nodules, 26 (37%) were classified as the nuclear atypia, and 45 (63%) as other atypia. The ACR TI-RADS score had a strong association with malignancy (p = 0.025). The presence and type of echogenic foci were associated with malignancy (p = 0.001). The malignancy rates for TR3, TR4, and TR5 nodules were 21%, 8%, and 55% respectively. CONCLUSION: The ACR TI-RADS was significantly associated with malignancy in both the overall AUS cohort and the nuclear atypia subgroup. The relatively high number of follicular thyroid carcinoma cases may have masked the predictive value of ultrasonography. The presence of peripheral calcifications was significantly associated with malignancy. Although the sample size was adequate by power analysis, larger cohorts would further strengthen these findings.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether intraoperative autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) reduces postoperative pain and haemorrhage and enhances wound healing after tonsillectomy, while critically evaluating the limitations that affect clinical translation and future applications. METHODS: Five databases were searched through 3 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing PRP with no PRP, placebo, or an untreated contralateral fossa. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty using GRADE. Random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used for pain and healing outcomes; sparse haemorrhage outcomes were analysed using Mantel-Haenszel common-effect models with sensitivity analyses. Parallel-group and split-mouth trials were analysed separately. RESULTS: Twelve randomized trials including 723 patients were included, with 11 contributing quantitative data. PRP was associated with reduced pain on postoperative day (POD) 1 (MD -1.21, 95% CI -2.01 to -0.40) and POD 3 (MD -1.12, 95% CI -2.10 to -0.14), although effects were heterogeneous and transient. Primary haemorrhage showed a favourable common-effect estimate (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.07-0.80), but this was based on only 12 events and was not confirmed by random-effects sensitivity analysis. Complete healing did not significantly differ between groups (RR 1.34, 95% CI 0.59-3.06). CONCLUSION: PRP may provide a modest early analgesic effect after tonsillectomy, but current evidence does not demonstrate a consistent improvement in haemostasis or mucosal healing. Future research should focus on standardized PRP characterization, patient-level comparative trials, and direct evaluation of whether PRP improves tissue regeneration compared with other biomaterial-based approaches.

item.title: Modified barbed reposition pharyngoplasty with symmetrical flap for acquired nasopharyngeal stenosis.
item.dc:creator: Okuno K, Chiba S, Capasso R, Honma A, Saito Y, Shimamura Y, Ikeda K, Ota F

Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867648



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Acquired nasopharyngeal stenosis (NPS) is a rare but serious complication following tonsillectomy or laser-assisted uvulopalatoplasty, leading to choking sensation and impaired nasal breathing. This study aimed to describe a modified pharyngoplasty technique and report its short-term outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on five patients with acquired NPS who underwent the procedure between 2017 and 2025. All cases were refractory to conservative treatment. The surgical technique involved symmetrical mucosal flaps combined with absorbable barbed sutures to achieve stable expansion of the pharyngeal airway. RESULTS: All patients showed rapid improvement in choking sensation and nasal breathing postoperatively. Normal speech and oral intake were possible from the day after surgery. During follow-up (5 months-2 years), no restenosis or major complications were observed, and endoscopic findings confirmed sustained airway patency. CONCLUSION: This technique can be performed safely in a single session without muscle resection or stenting and demonstrated favorable short-term outcomes. It may represent a practical surgical option for selected patients with acquired NPS. Further studies are required to confirm long-term efficacy.

item.title: Appropriate extent of endoscopic sinus surgery brings favorable therapeutic outcomes to chronic rhinosinusitis patients.
item.dc:creator: Tran T, Samuthpongtorn J, Seresirikachorn K, Chitsuthipakorn W, Hoang MP, Tran LV, Le MTQ, Anggraini D, Wardani RS, Mohamad S, et al.

Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867643



Abstract:
PURPOSE: The optimal extent of endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) remains undetermined. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative outcomes when the extent of ESS is concordant with the underlying pathophysiology. METHODS: This study enrolled 116 patients with CRS scheduled for three categories of ESS: limited ESS, full-house ESS, and extended ESS. Concordant ESS was defined as (1) limited ESS performed for patients requiring ventilation and drainage and (2) either full-house ESS or extended ESS performed for patients requiring access for topical therapies. Postoperative outcomes included symptom visual analogue scale (VAS), the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22), and endoscopic scores. RESULTS: At one year, patients receiving concordant ESS achieved superior outcomes in symptom VAS (mean difference [MD] 1.38; 95% CI 0.62-2.15; P < 0.01), SNOT-22 (MD 22.73; 95% CI 15.46-30.00; P < 0.01), and endoscopic scores (MD 6.48; 95% CI 1.96-11.00; P < 0.01). When ESS was performed to improve ventilation and drainage, limited ESS and full-house ESS brought comparable outcomes. Limited ESS achieved better outcomes than extended ESS in SNOT-22 (MD - 21.05; 95% CI - 38.72 to - 3.37; P = 0.02). When ESS aimed to provide access for topical therapies, SNOT-22 was greater improved by full-house (MD 21.32; 95% CI 10.01-32.62; P < 0.01) and extended ESS (MD 26.16; 95% CI 14.85-37.46; P < 0.01) compared to limited ESS. CONCLUSIONS: The extent of ESS should be tailored to the underlying pathophysiology. Limited and full-house ESS are appropriate to improve ventilation. Full-house and extended ESS provide better outcomes when access for topical therapies is required.

item.title: Gasless endoscopic thyroidectomy via the transsubclavian approach: comparable safety and superior anterior cervical function preservation.
item.dc:creator: Huang C, Wang W, Yao J
item.description:
Authors: Huang C, Wang W, Yao J
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10641-x
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867642



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional open thyroidectomy (COT) for papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) frequently induces anterior cervical dysfunction and conspicuous scarring. The gasless endoscopic thyroidectomy via the transsubclavian approach (GETTSA) offers technical simplicity and superior cosmesis. This study assessed whether GETTSA provides adequate completeness of resection and effectiveness compared with COT while achieving superior preservation of anterior cervical function. METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive patients with unilateral PTC who underwent hemithyroidectomy between 2023 and 2025, with 37 in the GETTSA group and 65 in the COT group. Baseline and perioperative data were prospectively collected. Scar appearance and anterior cervical function were assessed using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS), Neck Impairment Score (NIS), Swallowing Impairment Score (SIS), and Voice Impairment Score (VIS) at 1, 3, and 6 months. Group comparisons were performed using t‑tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, or chi‑square tests, and generalized estimating equations (GEE) evaluated longitudinal group, time, and interaction effects. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics between the two groups were comparable. GETTSA had a longer operative time (P < 0.001) but less intraoperative blood loss (P = 0.002); hospital stay was slightly longer (P < 0.001). Parathyroid autotransplantation rates were higher in GETTSA (P < 0.001), yet postoperative PTH and calcium levels were similar. GEE demonstrated significant group and time effects for VSS, NIS, and SIS (all P < 0.001), with significant group‑by‑time interactions (P = 0.048, P = 0.026, and P < 0.001, respectively), indicating better and faster recovery in the GETTSA group. VIS showed a significant time effect (P < 0.001), but no group effect (P = 0.333) or interaction (P = 0.637). R0 resection was achieved in all patients, and no major procedure‑related complications occurred. CONCLUSION: GETTSA offers superior functional and cosmetic outcomes-notably improved swallowing function, better scar appearance, and reduced neck discomfort-with less intraoperative bleeding, comparable parathyroid safety, and adequate completeness of resection. Long‑term oncological surveillance is ongoing.

item.title: Pediatric Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease and Otitis Media With Effusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the relationship between recurrent otitis media (ROM), chronic media otitis with effusion (COM), and laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD) in pediatric populations. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases. REVIEW METHODS: Two investigators independently screened papers with PRISMA guidelines considering the following primary outcomes: LPRD prevalence in pediatric ROM and COM, diagnostic methods used, and detection rates of gastroduodenal markers in middle ear effusions. Two random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate the pooled prevalence of pepsin/pepsinogen detection in middle ear effusions and to compare pepsin concentrations between COM/ROM patients and controls using standardized mean differences (Hedges' g). RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies were included (2070 pediatric patients). The cumulated gastroesophageal reflux disease prevalence in COM children was estimated to 50.7%, while 27.6% of children reported pharyngeal reflux events. Fifteen studies measured pepsin in effusions, reporting a pooled detection prevalence of 72.5% (95% CI: 53.7%-88.0%), rising to 85.6% with ELISA-based methods versus 17.9% with enzymatic assays. The pooled standardized mean difference in pepsin concentration between OME patients and controls was large and significant (Hedges' g = 1.92, 95% CI: 0.58-3.25, P = .005). Alkaline-activated gastroduodenal mediators were assessed in 3 studies, with detection rates ranging from 39.6% to 100% for trypsin and from 32% to 42% for bile salts. Substantial heterogeneity was found for COM/ROM and reflux disease diagnostic criteria, gastroduodenal biomarker measurements, and outcomes. CONCLUSION: Gastroduodenal biomarkers are present in middle ear effusions of children with COM and ROM. Future prospective transversal studies exploring alkaline-activated enzymes and bile salts in effusion of children with documented pharyngeal reflux events are needed.

item.title: Evaluation of Otolaryngology Residency and Faculty Demographics Following the Single Accreditation System.
item.dc:creator: Echevarria Cruz E, Hart S, Fioletova M, Smith A, Avirineni S, Rutt AL

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (OHNS) residency remains highly competitive, with persistent disparities in applicant representation. This study presents a cross-sectional analysis of OHNS residency and faculty demographics using 2025 program rosters, evaluating degree type (MD vs DO), geographic distribution, and leadership influence. STUDY DESIGN: A cross-sectional review. SETTING: All US ACGME-accredited OHNS residency programs, with data collected in 2024 to 2025. METHODS: Demographic data were collected on OHNS faculty and residents, including post-graduate year (PGY) 1 through PGY5 trainees at the time of data collection, corresponding to entry years from 2020 to 2024 across all US ACGME-accredited residency programs. Data was extracted from official program websites, FREIDA, ACGME, NRMP, and social media. Programs with incomplete data, those using the military match, and non-accredited sites were excluded. Descriptive statistics, χ2 tests, and correlation analyses were performed (p < .05). RESULTS: Of 131 programs, 125 were analyzed at the program level and 121 at the faculty level. DO residents were concentrated in Michigan (59%), Ohio (50%), and Oklahoma (50%). DO representation correlated with DO faculty (r = .82, p < .0001), DO program director (r = .95, p < .0001), and former AOA program designation (r = .92, p < .0001). A negative correlation existed between program size and DO resident (r = -.4, p < .0001). CONCLUSION: Despite growing diversity following the single accreditation system, disparities persist in OHNS. DO residents remain underrepresented and geographically concentrated, with representation strongly associated with osteopathic faculty presence, program leadership, and prior AOA affiliation.

item.title: Potential Benefit of Effective Implementation of Timely Postoperative Radiation for Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Luong PQ, Hartman AL, Velez-Velez LM, Mazul A, Massa ST
item.description:
Authors: Luong PQ, Hartman AL, Velez-Velez LM, Mazul A, Massa ST
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70484
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867218



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the potential benefit of survival of receiving timely postoperative radiation therapy (PORT) for head and neck cancer. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort. SETTING: National Cancer Database from 2004 to 2020. METHODS: Patients with a diagnosis of human papilloma virus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma who received adjuvant radiation were included. Exposure groups included timely PORT or delayed PORT (≤42 or >42 days from surgery to radiotherapy, respectively). The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival (OS). Inverse probability weighted models were used to estimate OS in the counter-factual scenario that all patients started radiation within 6 weeks while adjusting for confounding. Observed OS was for the entire cohort, while predicted OS was for the generated model of universal timely PORT within 6 weeks. Survival analyses were replicated for demographic and clinical subgroups. RESULTS: In total, 58,184 patients were included. Patients were mostly male, white, and non-Hispanic. The observed average 5-year OS was similar to the predicted OS (observed 0.58, 95% CI: 0.57-0.578; predicted 0.58, 95% CI: 0.57-0.59). The largest predicted benefit for timely PORT was seen in privately insured, white, rural, males, and with hypopharyngeal and stage IV cancer, though confidence intervals included the null hypothesis. Conversely, black patients were predicted to have a decline in OS with timely PORT (observed 0.54, 95% CI 0.53-0.56; predicted 0.50, 95% CI 0.46-0.52). CONCLUSION: For the overall cohort and other subgroups, even if optimally implemented, timely PORT is not predicted to improve OS. Modeling outcomes can guide resource allocation to the most impactful interventions.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This is a phase II subprotocol of the National Cancer Institute-Children's Oncology Group Pediatric Molecular Analysis for Therapy Choice (MATCH) precision oncology platform trial evaluating selpercatinib, a RET inhibitor, in children and young adults aged 1-21 years with relapsed or refractory solid tumors with RET alterations. item.title: Mitochondrially Encoded Cytochrome C Oxidase 1, a Hypoxia- and Lactylation-Related Gene, Acts as a Tumor Suppressor and Therapeutic Target in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zuo YD, Dong SD, Li JH, Li JC
item.description:
Authors: Zuo YD, Dong SD, Li JH, Li JC
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70475
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867034



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aberrant expression of mitochondrially encoded Cytochrome c Oxidase Subunit 1 (MT-CO1) has increasingly been associated with tumor invasiveness and adverse clinical outcomes across multiple malignancies. However, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remain poorly understood. METHODS: Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were integrated to identify genes consistently dysregulated across datasets. Candidate prognostic genes were subsequently prioritized using Cox proportional hazards regression in combination with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. A multi-omics validation framework was then applied, encompassing analysis of MT-CO1 expression in OSCC, protein-level validation using the Human Protein Atlas, and evaluation of associations with clinicopathological characteristics. The functional effects of MT-CO1 were evaluated in OSCC cell lines using gain-of-function assays. To assess the feasibility of pharmacologically targeting MT-CO1, molecular docking and subsequent molecular dynamics simulations were performed to characterize the interaction between amorolfine and MT-CO1; mechanistic rescue experiments were then conducted to determine whether the drug's effects were MT-CO1-dependent. RESULTS: MT-CO1 was associated with hypoxia and lactylation and was downregulated in OSCC, with lower expression correlating with poorer survival. MT-CO1 overexpression reduced cell viability, proliferation, and invasion while enhancing apoptotic signaling in vitro. Computational analyses further predicted a stable, high-affinity interaction between amorolfine and MT-CO1. Importantly, MT-CO1 suppression attenuated the antineoplastic effects of amorolfine in OSCC cells, supporting an MT-CO1-dependent mechanism of action. CONCLUSIONS: MT-CO1 as an underappreciated tumor-suppressive factor in OSCC and support further evaluation of amorolfine for therapeutic repurposing. MT-CO1 may serve as a biomarker of treatment response and that the MT-CO1-amorolfine axis may represent an actionable therapeutic vulnerability in OSCC.

item.title: Oral and Fecal Microbial Dysbiosis as Non-Invasive Diagnostic Biomarkers for Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, Yu H, Gao Y, Yang S, Wan S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, Yu H, Gao Y, Yang S, Wan S, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70779
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42865226



Abstract:
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including esophageal (EC), gastric (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), impose a substantial global burden, with early detection remaining crucial for improving patient outcomes. The oral and gut microbiota are increasingly implicated in cancer development and hold promise as sources of non-invasive biomarkers. However, current evidence on microbiome-based diagnostics remains fragmented, and a systematic comparison of the diagnostic accuracy between oral and fecal sampling across multiple GI cancer types is lacking. To address this gap, a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus up to December 31, 2025, identified 43 case-control studies (59 cohorts) comprising 4452 cancer patients and 5809 controls. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.846 (95% CI: 0.824-0.867), though with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 86.5%). By cancer type, pooled AUCs were 0.746 for EC (5 cohorts), 0.886 for GC (8 cohorts), and 0.850 for CRC (46 cohorts). A bivariate analysis of 20 cohorts comparing sample types found no statistically significant difference in diagnostic performance between oral (sAUC = 0.863) and fecal sampling (sAUC = 0.820; p = 0.369). While these exploratory findings suggest that oral and fecal microbial biomarkers may offer comparable diagnostic accuracy for GI cancers, with oral sampling presenting a more practical option for screening, the results are preliminary. Significant heterogeneity, a limited number of oral cohorts, and the absence of clinical control groups highlight the need for large-scale prospective studies with direct comparisons and real-world validation to validate these biomarkers for clinical translation.

Abstract:
Available epidemiological evidence shows that many cancers share familial risks, and this is increasingly confirmed by data on shared pathogenic germline gene variants between cancers. We decided to harness the world's largest resource on familial cancer to assess discordant familial risks for female breast (BC), prostate (PC), colorectal (CRC), and lung (LC) cancers with any of 22 different cancers in first-degree relatives (proband cancers). Familial relative risk was calculated as standardized incidence ratio (SIR) when either one proband or 2 or more (2+) probands were found in a family to distinguish low- and high-risk associations. Discordant familial associations of BC were significant for 12 1-proband and 5 2+ proband cancers. For PC, the numbers were 11 and 4; for CRC, they were 8 and 4; and for LC, they were 15 and 5. The results with large case numbers showed that BC, CRC, and LC associated with each other, but the familial association between PC and LC was negative. Many known or novel associations with possible genetic causes were found, including lobular BC with stomach cancer, PC with kidney cancer, CRC with squamous cell skin and thyroid cancers, and LC with gallbladder and endocrine tumors, the most common of which were parathyroid adenomas. Also, LC associations with esophageal and cervical cancers were unlikely to be due to smoking alone and require additional explanations. In conclusion, 2/3 of discordant associations could suggest low-risk genetic and environmental causation and 1/3 high-risk genetic causation, both waiting for experimental proof.

Abstract:

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy in patients with temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science until January 2026 to search for studies including patients with a diagnosis of intracapsular TMD as participants; physical therapy or physical therapy combined to other conservative approaches as intervention; placebo, sham treatments, oral pharmacological anti-inflammatory drugs, behavioral therapy, or other conservative approaches as comparison; maximal mouth opening (MMO) as outcome. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Odontogenic infections may progress to life-threatening complications if not managed promptly, and socioeconomic circumstances have been linked to their presentation, particularly where access to dental care is limited. Because every patient studied was already hospitalised, this analysis addresses the clinical type of infection at presentation, not the risk of developing one. METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cross-sectional review of hospital records was undertaken at the Allied Ward of Sunyani Teaching Hospital (January 2021 to January 2025). Of 811 consecutive admissions, 525 were excluded: 509 for non-odontogenic conditions and 16 for records missing more than 30% of required clinical fields, leaving 286 complete records. Chi-square tests were reported with Cramer's V and Monte Carlo exact p-values where cells were sparse. Because the unpenalised model showed quasi-complete separation, the primary analysis was a Firth-penalised multinomial logistic regression, with abscess as the reference outcome. RESULTS: Adjusting for age, sex, employment, residence, recorded oral hygiene, systemic comorbidity and alcohol use, unemployment was associated with higher adjusted odds of Ludwig's angina (LA) and not abscess (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI 1.27-6.09), and rural residence with necrotizing fasciitis (NF; AOR = 3.62, 95% CI 1.33-9.80). Systemic comorbidity was associated with LA (AOR = 4.14, 95% CI 1.83-9.36), NF (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI 2.95-25.75) and cellulitis (AOR = 2.07, 95% CI 1.03-4.18). Absence of a recorded poor-hygiene entry was associated with cellulitis (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI 2.42-26.83), interpreted as a documentation artefact not a protective effect. Sex and alcohol use showed no association. Number of children, the sole source of separation, was not retained; its penalised intervals included 1. CONCLUSION: Unemployment and systemic comorbidity were associated with more severe presentations, and rural residence with NF specifically. Findings are associational and describe variation in infection type among admitted patients rather than infection risk, within a retrospective single-centre design.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prospective study evaluated the impact of isthmus management (isthmus-sparing vs. isthmus-removing lobectomy) on postoperative hypothyroidism risk. METHODS: Between January 2022 and March 2023, 326 euthyroid patients with benign or low-risk papillary thyroid cancer were randomized into the isthmus-sparing (IS, n = 164) or isthmus-removing (IR, n = 162) group. RESULTS: TSH levels were significantly lower in the IS group at 3, 6, 12, and 18 months ( p < 0.05 ). Euthyroidism maintenance was higher in the IS group (62.2% vs. 38.9%, p = 0.001 ). item.title: Effects of Antimicrobial Mouthwashes on Oral Health and Blood Pressure: A Preliminary Parallel Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although antimicrobial mouthwashes vary in efficacy and safety for managing biofilm-induced gingivitis, concerns remain regarding their potential to reduce nitric oxide bioavailability and increase hypertension risk. Therefore, we investigated whether octenidine is more effective and causes fewer adverse events than chlorhexidine, and whether antimicrobial mouthwash use increases hypertension risk. METHODS: In this parallel randomized controlled trial, 90 participants were randomly allocated (1:1:1) to rinse with 10 mL of 2% saline (Group I), 0.2% chlorhexidine (Group II), or 0.1% octenidine (Group III) for 21 days. Co-primary outcomes (clinical parameters and blood pressure) and secondary outcomes (salivary bacterial count, adverse events, and pulse pressure) were assessed over 42 days. RESULTS: At day 22, antimicrobial mouthwashes significantly reduced clinical (29%-52%) and microbial (> 92%) measures (p < 0.001), whereas saline produced minimal changes (p > 0.05). Salivary nitrate levels showed the opposite trend. Groups II and III showed comparable efficacy, but octenidine was associated with fewer adverse events. Although systolic blood pressure increased slightly in all groups, the changes were clinically insignificant. Elevated pulse pressure in antimicrobial groups returned to baseline by Day 42. CONCLUSIONS: Octenidine (0.1%) was safer and comparably effective to chlorhexidine. Short-term antimicrobial mouthwash had no clinically significant effect on blood pressure. Authors: Menton SM, Fairweather D, Wilson FC, Zangerle DJ, Murphy EF, Darakjian AA, Thompson CC, Gajarawala SN, Knight DRT, Bruno KA, et al.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) or hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and inducible laryngeal obstruction (ILO) have more voice, cough, swallowing, GI issues, and MC activation than patients without ILO. METHODS: This retrospective study of 2162 patients meeting 2017 diagnostic criteria for hEDS (n = 507) or HSD (n = 1655) who were seen at the EDS Clinic in Mayo Clinic Florida from November 2019 to June 2025 compared patients who screened positive for ILO to those who screened negative. Patients were examined for self-reported symptoms of voice, cough, swallow, and GI issues as well as MC activation. RESULTS: Among patients with hEDS or HSD, 23.1% and 17.1% respectively screened positive for ILO. Patients with ILO had significantly more voice, cough, and swallow issues than patients without ILO (all p ≤ 0.007). Both diagnoses had more gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) (hEDS: 55.6% vs. 40.9%, p = 0.004; HSD: 55.8% vs. 42.2%, p < 0.0001). Additionally, both hEDS and HSD patients with ILO self-reported 18 allergy-related symptoms more often than those without ILO and had higher MC scores indicating widespread MC activation (all p < 0.0001). Cough, dysphagia, and elevated MC score were statistically significant predictors of ILO in both hEDS and HSD within a logistic regression analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Chronic cough, dysphagia, and elevated MC symptom burden were the strongest independent predictors of ILO across both hEDS and HSD, underscoring the need for routine multidisciplinary laryngeal assessment in this population.

item.title: Trajectories of Plasma Epstein-Barr Virus DNA and Clinical Outcomes in Recurrent or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Treated With PD-L1 Inhibitors: A Post-Hoc Analysis of a Multicenter, Phase II Study.

Authors: Pan Z, Pei Y, Diao J, Gao K, Ge J, Qing Y, Wei Y, Peng X

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable biomarkers for predicting clinical outcomes in patients with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (R/M NPC) treated with immunotherapy remain limited. This study evaluated the association between longitudinal EBV DNA trajectories and clinical outcomes in patients with R/M NPC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from a multicenter, single-arm, Phase II trial evaluating the programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor KL-A167 in patients with previously treated R/M NPC. Plasma EBV DNA was measured at baseline and at each scheduled efficacy assessment, which was conducted every six weeks until disease progression. EBV DNA trajectories were distinguished through a logistic trajectory model. Multivariable Cox models were used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for survival outcomes. RESULTS: We identified three distinct trajectories: persistently undetectable (n = 17, 13.8%), fluctuating (n = 40, 32.5%), and persistently detectable (n = 66, 53.7%). Compared with the persistently undetectable group, HRs of death were 4.96 (95% CI, 1.60-15.40) and 12.59 (95% CI, 4.01-39.51) for the fluctuating and persistently detectable groups, respectively. HRs of disease progression were 1.96 (95% CI, 0.97-3.96) and 3.22 (95% CI, 1.56-6.67), respectively. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that plasma EBV DNA trajectories could be a promising biomarker for monitoring treatment response and longitudinal risk stratification.

item.title: CyberKnife Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy for Reirradiation of Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Outcomes and Prognostic Factors.

item.description:
Authors: Sharon S, Qureshi MM, Keohan S, Luk S, Jang S, Truong MT
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70494

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is used for reirradiation in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (RM-HNSCC), but prognostic factors remain unclear. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 36 RM-HNSCC patients treated with CyberKnife-SBRT (2009-2022). ENDPOINTS: local control (LC) and overall survival (OS), estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 8.5 months, median OS was 9.6 months, with 1- and 2-year OS rates of 43.5% and 34.2%. One- and 2-year LC rates were 55.1% and 34.5%, with median time-to-recurrence of 14.1 months. On multivariable analysis, smoking > 30 pack-years predicted worse LC (HR 5.68; 95% CI, 1.42-22.70; p = 0.014), while former/never smoking predicted improved OS (HR 0.26; 95% CI, 0.08-0.82; p = 0.022). Gross tumor volume > 37.0 cm3 predicted worse LC (log-rank p = 0.044) and OS (p = 0.003) on univariate analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Smoking history independently predicted LC and OS; larger tumor volume was associated with worse outcomes and may inform patient selection for SBRT reirradiation.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated experience with probe-based near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) system (PTeye) in parathyroid gland (PTG) identification during total thyroidectomy. METHODS: In this retrospective study, patients undergoing total thyroidectomy using PTeye (2020-2022; n = 84) were compared with a historical visual-identification cohort (2018-2019; n = 103). RESULTS: PTG identification rates were comparable, although 42% of PTGs detected with PTeye were initially visualized with low or moderate confidence. Significantly fewer patients in the PTeye cohort had PTGs incidentally identified on histology (4.8% vs. 16.5%, p = 0.018), but there was no difference in the incidence of autotransplanted PTGs or total inadvertent parathyroidectomy. CONCLUSIONS: PTeye provides adjunctive confirmation of suspected parathyroid tissue, including glands initially identified with low or moderate visual confidence.

item.title: Hypoxia-induced HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling axis enhances proliferation of oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Wu K, Zhang S, Cao L, Wang J, Wang M, Zheng Z, Feng X
item.description:
Authors: Wu K, Zhang S, Cao L, Wang J, Wang M, Zheng Z, Feng X
Journal: British journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1038/s41416-026-03632-6
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860443



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypoxic microenvironment, a common feature of solid tumors, is critically involved in driving cancer malignancy. This research focuses on elucidating the function of high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), induced by such hypoxia, in the context of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). METHODS: We first profiled HMGB1 expression patterns in clinical OSCC specimens and evaluated their potential associations with clinicopathological parameters. To functionally characterize HMGB1, we conducted in vitro experiments utilizing silencing strategies. The impact of chronic cyclic hypoxia and HMGB1 depletion on key cellular processes-including proliferation, pyroptosis, and cell cycle-was systematically examined in OSCC cells. Signaling activity along the HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 axis was determined by immunoblotting. Furthermore, in vivo relevance was substantiated through murine xenograft models and a 4-NQO-induced carcinogenesis protocol. RESULTS: Analysis of clinical samples revealed that HMGB1 is constitutively upregulated in OSCC tissues. This elevated expression demonstrated a positive relationship with both increased tumor dimensions and lymph node metastasis. Subsequent Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that heightened HMGB1 levels are a marker for unfavorable patient outcomes. Furthermore, in cell culture systems, hypoxia treatment significantly elevates HMGB1 expression levels in OSCC cells. Knockdown of HMGB1 expression inhibits hypoxia-induced NLRP3, cleaved-caspase-1, and HIF-1α expression. Hypoxia treatment markedly enhanced OSCC cell proliferation, induced pyroptosis, and alleviated G2/M phase arrest, while HMGB1 knockdown reversed the pro-tumor effects of hypoxia. In vivo experiments demonstrated that HMGB1 knockdown inhibited tumor growth, whereas NLRP3 or caspase-1 deficiency delayed oral cancer progression. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggested that HMGB1 contributes to the progression of OSCC and has prognostic value. Targeting the hypoxia-induced HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling axis may offer a viable therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Regular post-treatment surveillance is associated with improved survival in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective study.
item.dc:creator: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, Kou J, Peng YF, Li-Lin, Ma J, Sun Y, Lv JW, Zhou GQ
item.description:
Authors: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, Kou J, Peng YF, Li-Lin, Ma J, Sun Y, Lv JW, Zhou GQ
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111818
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858857



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Benefit of post-treatment surveillance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), characterized by high recurrence risk, remains unexplored. We explored whether regular post-treatment surveillance facilitates earlier recurrence detection and improves survival. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We identified 8,798 patients with non-metastatic stage I-IVA NPC at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. The 1-year landmark analysis was chosen as representative of surveillance patterns, dividing patients into regular and irregular surveillance group based on surveillance intensity. Cox proportional hazards models clarified the association between overall survival (OS) and surveillance intensity, with subgroup analyses stratified by clinical stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA level. Survival impact of surveillance imaging for local, regional, and distant sites were also investigated. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 64.8 months. 1-year landmark analysis comprised 4,078 and 4,720 patients receiving regular (≥ 4 visits in the first year) and irregular surveillance (< 4 visits), respectively. Regular surveillance was linked to shorter median recurrence time (26.1 versus 27.0 months) and improved OS (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.99; P = 0.032) after multivariable adjustment. Notably, patients receiving regular imaging surveillance for distant site had better OS (HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.82; P < 0.001) whereas imaging for local (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.90-2.04; P = 0.140) and regional site (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.57-1.27; P = 0.428) did not. Regular surveillance patients with distant metastases exhibited fewer metastatic organs (P < 0.001) and earlier recurrence stages (P < 0.001), translating into prolonged post-recurrence survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Regular post-treatment surveillance, particularly distant imaging, could improve NPC survival, highlighting an urgency for evidence-based post-treatment surveillance strategies.

item.title: Evaluating imputation methods for longitudinal clinical trajectories: Toxicities in head and neck cancer treatment.
item.dc:creator: van der Hoek L, de Vette SPM, Neh H, MacRae DC, Langendijk JA, Sijtsema NM, van Ooijen PMA, van der Schaaf A, van Dijk LV
item.description:
Authors: van der Hoek L, de Vette SPM, Neh H, MacRae DC, Langendijk JA, Sijtsema NM, van Ooijen PMA, van der Schaaf A, van Dijk LV
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111815
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858855



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Longitudinally collected medical data is often afflicted by missingness, making methods mitigating missingness valuable. This study evaluated nine imputation methods for longitudinal data, using toxicity scores measured at multiple timepoints resulting from head and neck cancer treatment with radiotherapy. METHODS AND MATERIALS: For four toxicities (xerostomia, dysphagia, taste alteration, and sticky saliva), toxicity scores at 16 timepoints (1 prior, 7 during, and 8 after treatment) were collected, resulting in 1442 patients with on average ∼11.6 available timepoints. Imputation methods ranged from simple to deep learning-based. Methods were evaluated using a systematic removal strategy enabling comparison of true and imputed values. Patient-level, cohort-level and downstream model evaluation was done, evaluating inclusion criteria for patients, training data requirement and modelling effect respectively. RESULTS: General imputation quality showed minimal differences between methods, except simple methods, which performed worse. For patient-level evaluation, it was found that when patients had <50% of timepoints available, imputation started to worsen. Cohort-level evaluation showed that advanced methods could reach good performances at low patient counts (150 patients) but were more severely affected by low average timepoint availability. Downstream model evaluation showed negligible differences between methods, other than simple methods which resulted in different model coefficients. CONCLUSIONS: It was found that it is best to avoid simple imputation methods. Furthermore, when applying imputation to longitudinal data practitioners should be conscientious about inclusion of certain patients and if their dataset permits the use of more advanced imputation methods.

item.title: Dose-effect analysis of late dental adverse effects following radiation therapy in survivors of paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcoma.
item.dc:creator: Krommenhoek KB, Hol MLF, van der Aa N, Suttie M, Gaze MN, Wiersma J, Mandeville HC, Gillies C, Slater O, Bel A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Krommenhoek KB, Hol MLF, van der Aa N, Suttie M, Gaze MN, Wiersma J, Mandeville HC, Gillies C, Slater O, Bel A, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111820
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858853



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcomas (HNRMS) often require radiotherapy, causing dental complications during critical development. Limited literature suggests dose-dependent risks, but clear thresholds for late dental adverse effects are lacking. This study aims to characterize dose effects on developing dentition in paediatric HNRMS patients to identify dose-response relationships informing evidence-based treatment planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Orthopantomograms from survivors of HNRMS were evaluated using the validated DENTALE scoring system. Radiation doses from brachytherapy, external beam radiation with protons and photons to deciduous teeth were retrieved from treatment plans and converted to EQD2 (α/β = 3 Gy). Dose-response relationships were modelled per tooth using binary logistic regression in Mplus (COMPLEX option for within-patient dependency; model fit assessed by ROC analysis). RESULTS: Among 34 survivors (median age at diagnosis 5.6 years), 27 (79.4 %) exhibited late dental AE. Of 919 assessable permanent teeth, 242 (26.3 %) showed abnormalities. Increasing radiation dose was consistently associated with higher AE probability. The dose corresponding to 50 % predicted probability of any dental AE was 23 Gy(EQD2). Structure-specific thresholds were higher for crowns (68 Gy) and eruption disturbances (52 Gy(EQD2)), and lower for roots (24 Gy(EQD2)) and crown-root ratio abnormalities (36 Gy(EQD2)). CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates dose-effect relationships for radiation exposure of developing dentition, with clinically relevant structure-specific thresholds. Teeth receiving no radiation still show developmental abnormalities, likely due to chemotherapy. These findings support incorporating dentition as organ at risk and dose constraints into paediatric head-and-neck radiotherapy planning to reduce dental morbidity.

item.title: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma prevention in high-risk, resource-limited rural China: Dysplasia screening and modifiable risk factors in a 14-year follow-up study.
item.dc:creator: Pan D, Su M, Wang Y, Xu D, Han J, Wang X, Yan Q, Xu J, Wang N, Zhang Z, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Pan D, Su M, Wang Y, Xu D, Han J, Wang X, Yan Q, Xu J, Wang N, Zhang Z, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103248
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858638



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a major cause of cancer mortality in resource-limited regions, where barriers to screening, unsafe environmental exposures, and constrained health infrastructure hinder timely diagnosis and survivorship. METHODS: We conducted a 14-year follow-up study involving 11,397 adults from a rural high-risk area of Huai'an, China, integrating baseline endoscopic biopsy, epidemiological assessment, and dietary evaluations. The Cox regression model was used to assess the hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). FDR was used to account for multiple testing. RESULTS: During follow-up, 189 incident ESCC cases were identified. Histological severity of dysplasia strongly predicted progression, particularly severe dysplasia (HR=16.22; 95% CI: 8.42-31.25) and carcinoma in situ (HR=52.90; 95% CI: 26.29-106.46). Male sex, increasing age, lower BMI (especially female smokers), a family history of ESCC, consumption of shallow well or surface water, and very spicy diets were significantly associated with increased ESCC risk. Frequent intake of banana (HR=0.54; 95% CI: 0.39-0.76; P-FDR=0.014) and hawthorn (HR=0.58; 95% CI: 0.42-0.81; P-FDR=0.023) was significantly associated with reduced ESCC risk. CONCLUSIONS: Histological severity of dysplasia is a strong predictor of ESCC development. In addition, compared with historical cohorts lacking organized early diagnosis and treatment, progression rates observed in this population suggest that the region's screening program may have contributed to improved outcomes. While early detection and treatment remain essential, modifying environmental and dietary exposures may provide additional avenues for prevention. The results support integrated prevention strategies that combine endoscopic screening with feasible lifestyle interventions to reduce ESCC burden in high-risk communities.

item.title: Invasive Cervical Cancers After an HPV-Negative Test: Insights From HPV Testing Histories.
item.dc:creator: Hassan SS, Nordqvist Kleppe S, Asinger N, Wang J, Dillner J, Arroyo Mühr LS
item.description:
Authors: Hassan SS, Nordqvist Kleppe S, Asinger N, Wang J, Dillner J, Arroyo Mühr LS
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70783
Published: 2026-Oct-10

Abstract:
Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is the primary method for cervical screening, and a negative HPV test is associated with a very low subsequent risk of invasive cancer. Nevertheless, some cervical cancers are diagnosed following an HPV-negative test. Using Swedish registry data, we identified women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer between 2019 and 2024 and reconstructed HPV testing histories from the National Cervical Screening Registry. The HPV test closest to diagnosis, performed before or within 30 days after diagnosis, was defined as the index test. Of 3000 women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer, 243 (8.1%) had an HPV-negative index test. These women were older and more frequently diagnosed at advanced stages than women with an HPV-positive index test. After adjustment for age, calendar year, and histology, an HPV-negative index test remained associated with advanced-stage disease (adjusted OR 2.91, 95% CI: 2.13-4.00). Among women with an HPV-negative index test, 128 of 243 (52.7%) had no prior HPV testing recorded, 83 of 243 (34.2%) had consistently HPV-negative histories, and 32 of 243 (13.2%) had prior HPV positivity. Cytology records were available for 229 to 243 (94.2%), and 33 to 243 (13.6%) had a previous high-grade histopathological diagnosis. Among women with an HPV-negative index test, recurrent HPV positivity following an intervening negative test was observed in only one woman. Cervical cancers diagnosed after an HPV-negative test reflect heterogeneous HPV testing histories. Most women either had no prior HPV testing recorded or had consistently HPV-negative results, while HPV positivity was observed in a smaller subgroup.

item.title: Long-Term Outcomes of IDH2-Mutant Sinonasal Carcinomas Compared With IDH2-Wild Type Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Scholfield DW, Axiotakis L, Woods R, Tai K, Eagan A, Boe LA, Finnegan E, Tam K, Cracchiolo J, Dunn L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Scholfield DW, Axiotakis L, Woods R, Tai K, Eagan A, Boe LA, Finnegan E, Tam K, Cracchiolo J, Dunn L, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70495
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42855994



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal carcinomas are aggressive and often locally invasive at presentation, with no universally accepted treatment approach. Histopathologic IDH2-mutant status appears to be associated with improved treatment response and survival. However, the clinical significance of histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas, as well as that of IDH2 mutation status within SNUC, remains unclear and long-term clinical outcome data are limited. METHODS: Records from a prospectively maintained skull-base database at a large, tertiary care hospital system from 1986 to 2024 were reviewed. Patients with a diagnosis of SNUC or sinonasal tumor of any histopathology positive for IDH2 R172 mutation were identified. SMARCB1-deficient, SMARCA4-deficient, NUT sinonasal carcinomas, and other small round cell mimickers were excluded. After histopathologic confirmation, 22 IDH2-mutant SNUC, 14 IDH2-mutant non-SNUC, and 8 IDH2-wildtype SNUC cases were amenable to comprehensive clinicopathologic data review. A presence of IDH2 R172 and pathogenic TP53 mutations was determined by molecular testing and/or by immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 58 years and 61% of patients were male. The majority of patients presented with T4b disease (41% of IDH2-mutant SNUC; 57% of IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.3). There was no significant difference in the proportion of patients presenting with orbital invasion (55% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 64% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7) or intracranial invasion (82% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 79% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7). On histopathology, there was no significant difference in perineural invasion and margin status between the three subgroups (p > 0.6). A greater proportion of IDH2-mutant non-SNUCs had TP53 mutations (67%) than IDH2-mutant SNUC (31%) and IDH2-wildtype SNUC (29%) (p = 0.13). Across the cohort, 41% of patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with a partial response by RECIST criteria in 94% of patients across the subgroups. Median follow-up was 28 months (IQR 11-64 months). 5-year DSS of 73% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 75% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 80% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). 5-year RFS was 53% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 48% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 43% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). CONCLUSION: Upfront assessment of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients may be warranted to select patients for clinical trials with IDH-inhibitors. However, no significant differences in the extent of disease at presentation or response to induction chemotherapy were observed according to histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas or IDH2 mutation status within SNUC. Larger series are required to determine the prognostic significance of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients.

item.title: Study protocol: a phase II study of trifluridine/tipiracil plus liposomal irinotecan as second-line therapy in advanced biliary tract cancer (TRITICC 2).

Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-17089-6
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42875757



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognosis of patients with advanced biliary tract cancer progressing after gemcitabine-based first-line therapy remains poor. Effective second-line treatment options are limited, and outcomes with currently available regimens are modest. Trifluridine/tipiracil (FTD/TPI) and nanoliposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) have demonstrated clinical activity in gastrointestinal malignancies and may provide synergistic antitumor effects. METHODS: TRITICC-2 is an investigator-initiated, prospective, open-label, multicenter, single-arm phase II trial conducted at academic centers in Germany. The study evaluates the efficacy and safety of FTD/TPI in combination with nal-IRI in patients with histologically confirmed, unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer who have progressed on gemcitabine-based first-line therapy. A total of 38 patients are planned for enrollment. Treatment consists of oral FTD/TPI administered on days 1-5 combined with intravenous nal-IRI on day 1 of a 14-day cycle, continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints include overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), safety, and health-related quality of life. An optional translational research program includes serial liquid biopsies and biomarker analyses. Enrollment is ongoing, with recruitment initiated in late 2025. CONCLUSION: TRITICC-2 investigates a biologically rational combination of FTD/TPI and nal-IRI in a patient population with a high unmet medical need. The study is expected to provide prospective data on the clinical activity and safety of this regimen and may contribute to the identification of biomarkers associated with treatment response in advanced biliary tract cancer. item.title: Mohs vs. Wide Local Excision for Early-Stage (AJCC 0-II) Cutaneous Head and Neck Melanoma: A Meta-Analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Ardoin A, Vasudevan SS, Rodrigues KC, Vance CJ, Pou JD, Nathan CO
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70511
Published: 2026-Oct-09

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare oncologic outcomes of Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) versus wide local excision (WLE) in the management of cutaneous head and neck melanoma (CHNM), including melanoma in situ (MIS) and Stage I-II invasive disease. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science were systematically searched for studies published between January 2000 and March 2026 that reported outcomes of MMS versus WLE for CHNM, including MIS and AJCC Stage I-II invasive disease. Outcomes of interest were recurrence, tumor upstaging, and secondary excision rates, which were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis model. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness, and meta-regression was used to explore sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: Of 691 records screened, 23 studies comprising 7090 cases of early-stage (AJCC Stage 0-II) CHNM were included. The median age was 68.8 years, and 68.4% of patients were male. For MIS, the pooled local recurrence rate was lower after MMS (1.7%; 95% CI: 0.7-4.4) than after WLE (6.3%; 95% CI: 3.4-11.4). Upstaging to invasive melanoma was likewise less frequent with MMS (3.3%; 95% CI: 2.1-4.9) than with WLE (8.1%; 95% CI: 4.3-14.8), as was secondary surgical excision (1.2%; 95% CI: 0.1-10.3 vs. 9.7%; 95% CI: 3.0-27.0). Among Stage I-II cases, the pooled recurrence rate was 1.3% (95% CI: 0.3-4.6) after MMS and 8.8% (95% CI: 1.3-41.0) after WLE. CONCLUSION: Although none of the between-group differences reached statistical significance, MMS showed consistently favorable trends in local control and in reducing upstaging and secondary procedures for early-stage CHNM. These findings support consideration of MMS in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: Treatment pathways for oral tongue or floor of mouth reconstruction: A comparative analysis of islanded facial artery myomucosal flap and free anterolateral thigh flap.

Authors: Lin X, Han X, Wang M, Shao X, Du Z, Song B, Liu H
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108173
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42854362



Abstract:
PURPOSE: The free anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap is the mainstay for reconstructing intraoral defects after oral tongue (OT) or floor of mouth (FOM) squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) resection, but the islanded facial artery myomucosal (iFAMM) flap has emerged as an alternative for selected patients. This study compared perioperative outcomes, functional recovery, and hospitalization costs between the two reconstructive pathways in cT1-2 N0 OT/FOM SCC patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing resection of cT1-2 N0 OT/FOM SCC with reconstruction using either the iFAMM or free ALT flap. Baseline characteristics, operative duration, complications, functional outcomes (mouth opening, swallowing, speech), esthetic outcomes, and hospitalization costs were compared, with effect sizes (95% CI) and multivariable regression adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: Among 31 patients, 16 received iFAMM flap-based pathway treatment (iFAMM pathway) and 15 received free ALT flap-based pathway treatment (ALT pathway). While functional outcomes were comparable, the iFAMM pathway showed shorter operative time (514.4 ± 66.2 vs. 602.6 ± 95.2 min, p = 0.005), higher aesthetic VAS score (6.8 ± 1.5 vs. 4.9 ± 1.3, p = 0.001), and lower costs (8,848.7 ± 2,075.1 USD vs. 14,212.5 ± 2,719.9 USD, p < 0.0001). Multivariable regression confirmed flap-based pathway as an independent predictor for all the three primary outcomes. CONCLUSION: The iFAMM pathway appears to be a promising alternative to the ALT pathway for surgical treatment of cT1-2 N0 OT/FOM SCC with comparable function, superior aesthetics, and lower costs. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in prospective trials.

item.title: Phase I/II Study of Bavdegalutamide, a Proteolysis-Targeting Chimera Androgen Receptor Degrader, in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Gao X, Garmezy B, Vuky J, Shen J, Sartor O, Sternberg CN, Dreicer R, Hussain M, Rezazadeh Kalebasty A, Percent IJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Gao X, Garmezy B, Vuky J, Shen J, Sartor O, Sternberg CN, Dreicer R, Hussain M, Rezazadeh Kalebasty A, Percent IJ, et al.

Published: 2026-Oct-09
